rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may end at “victorious,” making “there the authority belongs to God” a separate sentence.
rows.anchor: وهذه جملة منقطعة عما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one parsing, an implicit verb such as “was established” makes الولاية the subject governed by هنالك; لله may attach to استقرار, the adverb, الولاية, or be an omitted circumstantial predicate under al-Akhfash’s view.
rows.anchor: فالولاية فاعل بالظرف قبلها، أي: استقرت الولاية لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, هنالك is an adverb attached to the predicate لله, to what لله depends on, to الولاية, or to an omitted circumstantial predicate governed by an abstract استقرار.
rows.anchor: منصوبا على الظرف متعلقا بخبر " الولاية " وهو " لله "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third parse makes هنالك the predicate and لله an additional complement, with the same governor proposed in the first analysis.
rows.anchor: أن يجعل " هنالك " هو الخبر، و " لله " فضلة

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: He treats هنالك as completing the preceding clause, governed by منتصرا and pointing to the afterlife; the pause after هنالك is then complete and الولاية لله begins a new nominal sentence.
rows.anchor: وإليه نحا أبو إسحاق. وعلى هذا فيكون الوقف على " هنالك " تاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense of هنالك retains its locative meaning.
rows.anchor: أنه على موضوعه من ظرفية المكان كما تقدم معناه.

rows.speaker: الأخوان
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamza read الولاية with kasra, unlike the majority’s fatḥa; the distinction was treated under al-Anfāl and is not repeated here.
rows.anchor: وتقدم أن الأخوين يقرآن " الولاية " بالكسر، والفرق بينها وبين قراءة الباقين بالفتح

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو والأصمعي
rows.claim: They call the kasra in الولاية incorrect because faʿāla usually denotes a craft or an attribute one assumes, whereas this verse is not about administering affairs.
rows.anchor: وحكي عن أبي عمرو والأصمعي أن كسر الواو هنا لحن.

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو والكسائي
rows.claim: They read الحق in the nominative: it can modify الولاية, predicate an implicit هو referring to what was revealed, or be a subject with an implicit predicate meaning “that is the truth.”
rows.anchor: والرفع، من ثلاثة أوجه، أحدها: أنه صفة للولاية.

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The majority read الحق in the genitive as an adjective of the divine name.
rows.anchor: والجر على أنه صفة للجلالة الكريمة.

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي وأبو حيوة وعمرو بن عبيد ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read الحق in the accusative as an emphatic verbal noun confirming the sentence’s meaning.
rows.anchor: نصبا على المصدر المؤكد لمضمون الجملة

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة
rows.claim: They read عقبا with a sukūn on qāf, while the rest use ḍamma; the source reports dialectal and easing explanations for the vowel difference, noting one proposed reversal is unusual.
rows.anchor: عاصم وحمزة بسكون القاف، والباقون بضمها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ثوابا, عقبا, and أملا are accusative specification nouns governed by the preceding comparative forms.
rows.anchor: على التمييز لأفعل التفضيل قبلها.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He reports a reading عقبى with final alif, a verbal noun like بشرى, transmitted from ʿĀṣim.
rows.anchor: بالألف وهي مصدر أيضا كبشرى، وتروى عن عاصم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يوم may be governed by an implicit “we say” followed by لقد جئتمونا, by an implicit اذكر, or coordinated with عند ربك under خير.
rows.anchor: منصوب بقول مضمر بعده تقديره: نقول لهم نسير الجبال:

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
rows.claim: They read the verb passively, with الجبال as نائب الفاعل; the agent is omitted because it is known as God or angels acting on His command.
rows.anchor: بضم التاء وفتح الياء مبنيا للمفعول. " الجبال " بالرفع لقيامه مقام الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passive reading agrees with 78:20 and is supported by ʿAbd Allāh’s passive past-tense reading here.
rows.anchor: وهذه القراءة موافقة لما اتفق عليه في قوله

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: They read نسير with the first-person plural and the mountains as its direct object; this fits the following وحشرناهم.
rows.anchor: بالنصب على المفعول به، وهذه القراءة مناسبة لما بعدها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He follows the passive reading but uses a yāʾ for the verb because the feminine gender is grammatical rather than natural.
rows.anchor: ابن كثير ومن ذكر معه إلا أنه بالياء من تحت لأن التأنيث مجازي.

rows.speaker: ابن محيصن ومحبوب عن أبي عمرو
rows.claim: They read تسير with an open tāʾ from سار تسير, making الجبال its nominative subject.
rows.anchor: ورواها محبوب عن أبي عمرو: " تسير " بفتح التاء من فوق ساكن الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بارزة is a circumstantial accusative because ترى denotes visual perception.
rows.anchor: " بارزة " حال؛ إذ الرؤية بصرية.

rows.speaker: عيسى
rows.claim: He reads ترى passively, with الأرض as the نائب الفاعل.
rows.anchor: مبنيا للمفعول، و " الأرض " قائمة مقام الفاعل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وحشرناهم may be a past form used for future events, as with عرضوا and وضع الكتاب.
rows.anchor: ماض مراد به، المستقبل، أي: ونحشرهم، وكذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the wāw introduces a circumstantial clause: the mountains are moved while people are being gathered so they witness the terrors.
rows.anchor: أن تكون الواو للحال، والجملة في محل النصب، أي: نفعل التسيير

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He says the past tense signals that the gathering precedes the mountain-moving and the earth’s exposure, letting people witness the great terrors.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على أن حشرهم قبل التسيير وقبل البروز ليعاينوا تلك الأهوال العظام

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: He prefers the circumstantial wāw analysis and gives an account like the author’s preceding explanation.
rows.anchor: " والأولى أن تكون الواو للحال " فذكر نحوا مما قدمته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مغادرة here means leaving or abandoning; its verb form does not imply reciprocal action. The related words غدر and غدير are explained through the sense of leaving.
rows.anchor: بمعن الغذر وهو الترك، أي: فلم نترك. والمفاعلة هنا ليس فيها مشاركة.

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: His cited line uses غدائره for long hair left to grow, illustrating غديرة and its plural غدائر.
rows.anchor: والغديرة: الشعر الذي ترك حتى طال. والجمع غدائر.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He reads فلم تغادر with tāʾ; its subject may be the earth or an understood noun from the context.
rows.anchor: بالتاء من فوق، والفاعل ضمير الأرض

rows.speaker: أبان
rows.claim: He reads يغادر passively and makes أحد nominative.
rows.anchor: " يغادر " مبنيا للمفعول، " أحد " بالرفع.

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: He reads نغدر with ḍamma on nūn, sukūn on ghayn, and kasra on dāl, from أفعل meaning غدر.
rows.anchor: بضم النون وسكون العين وكسر الدال من " أغدر بمعنى غدر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صفا is a circumstantial accusative from a verbal noun, then used for a group standing in rows.
rows.anchor: حال من مرفوع " عرضوا " وأصله المصدرية.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: صفا may be a singular standing for plural صفوفا; two hadiths describe people gathered in rows and the people of Paradise in 120 rows, of which this community forms 80.
rows.anchor: مفرد وقع موقع الجمع، إذ المراد صفوفا، ويدل عليه الحديث الصحيح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, صفا صفا is understood by ellipsis, as in 89:22 and 78:38, where the repeated صفا is expressed or supplied.
rows.anchor: ثم حذف، أي: صفا صفا. ومثله قوله في موضع:

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view is that all creatures stand in a single row, which is more striking as a display of divine power.
rows.anchor: بل كل الخلائق يكونون صفا واحدا، وهو أبلغ في القدرة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith descriptions can reflect different moments during the long Day, when people are sometimes in one row and sometimes in rows; 70:4 gives its duration as fifty thousand years.
rows.anchor: لأنه يوم طويل كما شهد له بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لقد جئتمونا can follow an implicit “we said,” which also governs يوم نسير الجبال in 18:47; alternatively it is an implicit circumstantial statement describing those presented.
rows.anchor: أي: وقلنا لهم: كيت وكيت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كما خلقناكم means arriving as at the first creation: barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, without property or children; al-Zamakhsharī paraphrases it as being raised as first created.
rows.anchor: حفاة عراة غرلا، لا مال ولا ولد معكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under both proposed explanations, كما خلقناكم describes an omitted verbal noun; on Sībawayh’s analysis it is circumstantial from that noun’s pronoun.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذين التقديرين، يكون نعتا للمصدر المحذوف، وعلى رأي سيبويه يكون حالا من ضميره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن is the lightened particle; negation separates it from its clause because the predicate is a regular inflected clause, not a prayer.
rows.anchor: وفصل بينها وبين خبرها لكونه جملة متصرفة غير دعاء بحرف النفي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لكم may be the second object of جعل meaning “make,” with موعد as the first; alternatively it attaches to جعل or is circumstantial from موعد when جعل means simple creation.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون مفعولا ثانيا للجعل بمعنى التصيير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بل in بل زعمتم marks a transition without cancelling the preceding statement.
rows.anchor: لمجرد الانتقال من غير إبطال.

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The common reading makes وضع passive; Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads it actively, with God or an angel as subject and الكتاب as object.
rows.anchor: وزيد بن علي على بنائه للفاعل، وهو الله أو الملك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الكتاب is generic and singular because each person is understood to have an individual record.
rows.anchor: جنس للكتب؛ إذ من المعلوم أن لكل إنسان كتابا يخصه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He refers to an earlier discussion of pausing at مال هذا الكتاب and the written separation of the preposition in 4:78.
rows.anchor: وكيف فصلت لام الجر من مجرورها خطا في سورة النساء عند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لا يغادر is a circumstantial clause describing the book; its governor is the preceding prepositional phrase standing in for a verb, or the underlying state it depends on.
rows.anchor: والعامل الجار والمجرور لقيامه مقام الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إلا أحصاها may be an adjective of صغيرة وكبيرة, or the second object of يغادر because ترك can take two objects; a cited verse of poetry illustrates that usage.
rows.anchor: و " يترك " قد يتعدى لاثنين كقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poetic example has تركتك governing ذا مال and ذا نشب as two objects; the poet is not identified in this excerpt.
rows.anchor: فقد تركتك ذا مال وذا نشب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وإذ قلنا means “remember when We said.”
rows.anchor: قوله: { وإذا قلنا }: أي: اذكر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كان من الجن is best read as a fresh explanatory sentence answering an implied question; Abū al-Baqāʾ’s circumstantial reading with an implicit قد is less evident.
rows.anchor: أظهرهما: أنه استئناف يفيد التعليل جوابا لسؤال مقدر.

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: He treats كان من الجن as circumstantial, with قد understood; the author says this reading is not clear.
rows.anchor: قاله أبو البقاء وليس بالجلي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The causal force of فـ in ففسق is clear: his being one of the jinn led to his disobedience.
rows.anchor: السببية في الفاء ظاهرة، تسبب عن كونه من الجن الفسق.

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: He explains the fāʾ as meaning “Iblīs refused, so he sinned”; the author accepts a distant paraphrase where كان من الجن stands for امتنع but rejects positing an omitted verb as unnecessary.
rows.anchor: فيحتمل مع بعده، وإن عنى أنه حذف فعل عطف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عن in فسق عن أمر retains its normal sense of going beyond; the alternative takes it as باء, “because of His command.”
rows.anchor: على بابها من المجاوزة، وهي متعلقة ب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wāw in وذريته is most naturally coordinative, though it may mean “with.” من دوني may attach to taking or modify أولياء through an omitted phrase.
rows.anchor: يجوز في الواو أن تكون عاطفة وهو الظاهر، وأن تكون بمعنى مع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وهم لكم عدو is circumstantial either from the object of اتخذتم or its subject; its linking pronoun permits both.
rows.anchor: جملة حالية من مفعول الاتخاذ أو فاعله؛ لأن فيها مصححا لكل من الوجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In بئس, the subject is implicit and explained by its specification; the condemned item is omitted and understood as Iblīs and his offspring.
rows.anchor: فاعلها مضمر مفسر بتمييزه. والمخصوص بالذم محذوف تقديره: بئس البدل إبليس وذريته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: للظالمين may modify an omitted circumstantial phrase from بدلا or attach to the verb of condemnation.
rows.anchor: من " بدلا ". وقيل: متعلق بفعل الذم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ما أشهدتهم may refer to Iblīs and his offspring, to the angels, to the disbelievers, or to all creation; the latter readings challenge worship or attribution without witness.
rows.anchor: أي: إبليس وذريته، أو ما أشهدت الملائكة فكيف تعبدونهم؟

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وشيبة والسختياني
rows.claim: They and other readers read أشهدناهم with the plural of majesty.
rows.anchor: في آخرين: " أشهدناهم " على التعظيم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: المضلين replaces an implicit pronoun, referring to those denied witnessing creation; naming their blameworthy quality stresses their bad character.
rows.anchor: وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر؛ إذ المراد بالمضلين

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The common reading has كنت with a ḍamma, reporting God’s speech; al-Ḥasan, al-Jaḥdarī, and Abū Jaʿfar use fatḥa to address the Prophet.
rows.anchor: إخبارا عنه تعالى. وقرأ الحسن والجحدري وأبو جعفر بفتحها

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: He reads متخذ with nūn as an active participle governing المضلين in the accusative, for a present or future sense.
rows.anchor: نون اسم الفاعل ونصب به، إذ المراد به الحال أو الاستقبال.

rows.speaker: عيسى
rows.claim: He reads عضدا with fatḥa on ʿayn and sukūn on ḍād, a common easing; Tamīm usage of سبع and رجل is cited as a parallel.
rows.anchor: بفتح العين وسكون الضاد، وهو تخفيف شائع كقول تميم:

rows.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan has several other vowel forms of عضدا, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk reads ʿayn with kasra and ḍād with fatḥa; these are dialect forms.
rows.anchor: والضحاك " عضدا " بكسر العين وفتح الضاد. وهذه لغات في هذا الحرف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عضد means the human or animal forearm and figuratively means helper or supporter, as in 28:35.
rows.anchor: ويعبر به عن العون والنصير فيقال: فلان عضدي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يوم is governed by اذكر: remember the day when We say this will happen.
rows.anchor: أي: ويوم نقول يجري كيت وكيت.

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: He reads نقول with the first-person plural, matching ما أشهدتهم; the other readers use third-person ياء because God’s name was just mentioned.
rows.anchor: بنون العظمة مراعاة للتكلم في قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: موبقا may be the first object of جعل with the preposed phrase between them as second; alternatively جعل takes one object and the phrase attaches to it or circumstantially modifies موبقا.
rows.anchor: مفعول أول للجعل، والثاني الظرف المقدم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: موبق means ruin or destruction, with the verb used for perishing and for a sin bringing destruction.
rows.anchor: الموبق: المهلك، يقال: وبق يوبق وبقا، أي: هلك

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He interprets the phrase as God making their connection a ruin, taking البين to mean connection rather than a locative interval; on this parse بينهم is the first object and موبقا the second.
rows.anchor: فجعل البين بمعنى الوصل، وليس بظرف كقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: موبقا is apparently a verbal noun, though it may denote a place.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون مصدرا وهو الظاهر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مصرف means a turning aside or place of escape; it may also be a place or time noun.
rows.anchor: قوله: { مصرفا }: المصرف: المعدل.

rows.speaker: الهذلي
rows.claim: The cited Hudhayl verse uses مصرف to ask whether there is any way to turn aside from Shaybah.
rows.anchor: أزهير هل عن شيبة من مصرف

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: He says مصرف means انصرافا and may be a place noun; the author calls the verbal-noun analysis mistaken because this pattern’s source has fatḥa, while its time and place nouns have kasra.
rows.anchor: وهذا سهو فإنه جعل المفعل بكسر العين مصدرا لما مضارعه

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: He reads مصرفا with fatḥa on rāʾ as a verbal noun; the author regrets that Abū al-Baqāʾ did not cite this reading to support his point.
rows.anchor: بفتح الراء جعله مصدرا؛ لأنه مكسور العين في المضارع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من كل may modify an omitted noun that is the object of صرفنا, meaning a parable from every kind; alternatively, Akhfash and the Kufans treat من as extra.
rows.anchor: صفة لموصوف محذوف، وهو مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جدلا is an accusative specification noun.
rows.anchor: " جدلا " منصوب على التمييز.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أكثر شيء means people exceed all disputants in argument when the disputing things are considered individually; singular شيء stands for plural things.
rows.anchor: أكثر الأشياء التي يتأتى منها الجدال إن فصلتها واحدا واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible analysis derives جدلا from the original subject of كان, with the underlying wording “the human’s disputation was the greatest thing”; the author sees difficulty in this.
rows.anchor: من اسم كان إذ الأصل: وكان جدل الإنسان أكثر شيء؟ فيه نظر.

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: He offers two explanations: شيء means disputant, since a comparative is related to a category it partly belongs to; or omitted wording is جدل الإنسان and جدلا specifies it.
rows.anchor: شيئا هنا في معنى مجادل؛ لأن أفعل يضاف إلى ما هو بعض له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second estimate needs a further metaphor: one must attribute disputation to disputation itself, like شعر شاعر, to say human disputation exceeds other disputation.
rows.anchor: وهو أن تتجوز فتجعل للجدل جدلا كقولهم:

none: Only points back to earlier discussions of وما منع and the readings and interpretation of قبلا; no analysis is restated here.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ليدحضوا attaches to يجادل; الإدحاض means making something slip or removing it from its place, as with a slipping foot or an unstable argument.
rows.anchor: والإدحاض: الإزلاق يقال: أدحض قدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet’s line illustrates the root through a camel turning aside on slippery mud; the source also links دحض with clay and a place called دحض.
rows.anchor: وحدت كما حاد البعير الدحض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما in وما أنذروا may be a verbal noun or a relative pronoun with its antecedent omitted; either way it is coordinated with آياتي.
rows.anchor: هذه أن تكون مصدرية، وأن تكون بمعنى الذي والعائد محذوف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هزوا may be the second object or a circumstantial accusative; prior discussions of its readings and the remaining syntax are not repeated.
rows.anchor: مفعول ثان أو حال. وتقدم الخلاف في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: موعد may be a verbal noun, a time noun, or a place noun.
rows.anchor: أن يكون مصدرا أو زمانا أو مكانا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: موئل is a refuge or return, from وأل يئل meaning to return; here the author takes it as a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: المرجع من وأل يئل، أي: رجع، وهو من التأويل.

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ interprets الموئل as salvation and cites al-Aʿshā’s ما يئل to mean “does not escape.”
rows.anchor: المنجى، وألت نفسه، أي: نجت

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: He glosses الموئل as a refuge or place of recourse and explains the related verb as seeking refuge.
rows.anchor: يقال: وأل فلان إلى فلان يئل وألا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من دونه attaches to the verb of finding, which takes one object, or is an omitted circumstantial phrase modifying موئلا.
rows.anchor: متعلق بالوجدان لأنه متعد لواحد، أو بمحذوف

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر والزهري
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads مولا with only a kasra on wāw; al-Zuhrī doubles the wāw. The former is more regular as an eased form.
rows.anchor: بواو مسكورة فقط. والزهري: بواو مشددة فقط.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وتلك القرى may be subject and predicate with أهلكناهم as a second predicate or circumstantial clause; alternatively القرى is an adjective, explanation, or apposition and أهلكناها is the predicate; or تلك is governed by an omitted verb.
rows.anchor: حينئذ: إما خبر ثان أو حال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in أهلكناهم refers to the omitted أهل in “the people of those towns,” not directly to القرى.
rows.anchor: المضاف إلى القرى، إذ التقدير: وأهل تلك القرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لما may be a particle or a temporal adverb.
rows.anchor: حرفا، وأن يكون ظرفا وقد عرف ما فيها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings of لمهلكهم vary: ʿĀṣim has fatḥa on mīm, the rest ḍamma; Ḥafṣ has kasra on lām and the rest fatḥa, yielding three combinations.
rows.anchor: مع فتح اللام، وهي رواية أبي بكر عنه.

rows.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: His reading with both mīm and lām fatḥa makes مهلك a verbal noun annexed to its subject; Abū ʿAlī also allows annexation to the object.
rows.anchor: فيها مصدر مضاف لفاعله. وجوز أبو علي

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: He argues that هلك can be transitive without hamza and cites a poetic line with هالك من تعرجا; the author says the verse does not prove this because it can be an adjective construction.
rows.anchor: وقد منع الناس ذلك وقالوا: لا دليل في البيت لجواز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The line can be parsed like حسن الوجه: من تعرجا is the raised complement of هالك, with an understood pronoun for مهمه, rather than a direct object.
rows.anchor: ثم أضمر في " هالك " ضمير " مهمه "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No accusative reconstruction is needed if هالك is treated as an adjective, which may be annexed to its raised complement; this depends on allowing a relative noun in adjective position, which the author says is correct.
rows.anchor: والصفة المشبهة تضاف إلى مرفوعها، إلا أن هذا مبني على خلاف آخر

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: He calls Abū Bakr’s reading a time noun only; the author finds this surprising because the form can also be a verbal noun, and distinguishes source from time/place by the vowel pattern.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكر غيره. وجوز غيره فيه الزمان والمصدر.

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: He allows مهلك in Abū Bakr’s reading to be a verbal noun despite the unusual kasra, comparing it to المرجع.
rows.anchor: وشذ فيه الكسر كالمرجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If this reading is a verbal noun, the question whether it is annexed to its subject or object follows the same debate as before.
rows.anchor: وإذا قلنا إنه مصدر فهل هو مضاف لفاعله أو مفعوله؟

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: Their reading with ḍamma on mīm and fatḥa on lām may be a verbal noun annexed to its object or a time noun; interpreting it as the destroyed person or group is unlikely.
rows.anchor: ويبعد أن يراد به المفعول، أي: وجعلنا للشخص أو الفريق المهلك منهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the remaining reading, مهلك may be a verbal noun or a time noun; موعد likewise is a verbal noun or time noun.
rows.anchor: وأما قراءة الباقين فواضحة. و " مهلك " فيها يجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذ is accusative under an implicit اذكر, or it marks the time when Moses said to his attendant what has been recounted.
rows.anchor: أو وقت قال لفتاه جرى ما قصصنا عليك من خبره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لا أبرح may be defective and require a predicate, or complete and need no predicate.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أن تكون ناقصة فتحتاج إلى خبر. والثاني: أن تكون تامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If defective, its omitted predicate may be أسير, though grammarians disallow predicate omission even when implied except in poetic necessity; a cited line exemplifies the exception.
rows.anchor: نص بعض النحويين على أنه لا يجوز ولو بدليل، إلا في ضرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second defective-verb analysis supplies the noun مسير: “my journey will not cease until I reach”; the author says al-Zamakhsharī blends this with the omitted-predicate analysis.
rows.anchor: حذف مضاف تقديره: لا يبرح مسيري حتى أبلغ

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He reads لا أبرح as لا أزال with an omitted predicate inferred from the journey and حتى أبلغ, and offers a second, elegant analysis with مسيري as the subject.
rows.anchor: هي بمعنى لا أزال، وقد حذف الخبر لأن الحال والكلام معا يدلان عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second analysis leaves the clause حتى أبلغ without a pronoun linking it back to مسيري; a possible repair is an omitted به, “until I reach by it.”
rows.anchor: من رابط يربطها به. ألا ترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If لا أبرح is complete, it means “I remain at my course,” persisting in travel and seeking; this analysis also needs an omitted object, so ellipsis is required in either construction.
rows.anchor: بمعنى ألزم المسير والطلب، ولا أفارقه ولا أتركه

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: They read مجمع with fatḥa as the place of meeting, though it may be a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: بفتح الميم وهو مكان الاجتماع، وقيل: مصدر.

rows.speaker: الضحاك وعبد الله بن مسلم بن يسار
rows.claim: They read مجمع with kasra; the author calls it anomalous because the present verb has fatḥa on its middle root letter.
rows.anchor: بكسرها، وهو شاذ، لفتح عين مضارعه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حقبا is an adverb for a long period; reported durations include eighty years, one year in Quraysh usage, and seventy years.
rows.anchor: منصوب على الظرف وهو بمعنى الدهر. وقيل: ثمانون سنة.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He reads حقبا with a sukūn on qāf, either as easing or as an independent dialect; its plural is أحقاب, and the source gives related forms for حقبة.
rows.anchor: بإسكان القاف فيجوز أن يكون تخفيفا، وأن يكون لغة مستقلة.

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: His line uses حقبة, illustrating the related word for a period.
rows.anchor: فإن تنأ عنها حقبة لا تلاقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أو أمضي is most naturally coordinated with أبلغ, offering two alternatives: reaching the meeting place or travelling for a long period.
rows.anchor: يعني بأحد أمرين: إما ببلوغه المجمع، أو بمضيه حقبا.

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: He allows أو to mean “except that,” with أن امضي describing a period long enough to know the meeting place was missed.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكره أبو البقاء معنى صحيح، فأخذ الشيخ هذا المعنى

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: He instead takes أو as إلى and makes the journey’s endpoint both a place and a time; the author objects that both endpoints must then be reached, unlike the intended meaning.
rows.anchor: فيكون الفعل المنفي قد غيي بغايتين مكانا وزمانا، فلا بد من حصولهما معا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading attributes forgetting to both Moses and his attendant: they forgot to check the fish, which was their sign.
rows.anchor: الظاهر نسبة النسيان إلى موسى وفتاه، يعني نسيا تفقد أمره، فإنه كان علامة لهما

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, Moses forgot to tell the attendant to bring the fish, and Joshua forgot to remind him.
rows.anchor: نسي موسى ان يأمره بالإتيان به ونسي يوشع أن يفكره بأمره.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third reading says Joshua alone forgot, with “one of them” understood through an omitted noun, as in the statement about pearls and coral in 55:22.
rows.anchor: وهو على حذف مضاف، أي: نسي أحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سربا is the second object of اتخذ; في البحر may attach to اتخذ or be circumstantial from either object.
rows.anchor: وأن يتعلق بمحذوف على أنه حال من المفعول الأول أو الثاني.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both the pronoun in سبيله and the unexpressed subject of اتخذ refer to the fish.
rows.anchor: وكذا المرفوع في " اتخذ ".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جاوزا has an omitted object, either the appointed stopping place or the meeting of the two seas.
rows.anchor: أي: جاوزا الموعد. وقيل: جاوزا مجمع البحرين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هذا points to the journey undertaken after they passed the appointed place or the meeting place.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى السفر الذي وقع بعد مجاوزتهما الموعد، أو مجمع البحرين.

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The common reading vowels نصبا with fatḥa on both letters; ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr uses ḍamma on both, among four dialect forms reported by Abū al-Faḍl al-Rāzī.
rows.anchor: العامة على فتح النون والصاد. وعبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: He says أرأيت has been repurposed: when it means “tell me,” Arabs may drop hamza and require the address suffix, whereas “did you see” keeps hamza; its syntax differs by sense.
rows.anchor: بحذف الهمزة إذا كانت بمعنى اخبرني، وإذا كانت بمعنى ابصرت لم تحذف همزتها.

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: He explains أرأيت إذ أوينا ... فإني as “now, when we took shelter, I forgot,” with the fāʾ introducing the response; إذ alone cannot function as a conditional without ما.
rows.anchor: فما دخلت الفاء إلا وقد اخرجت إلى معنى: أما أو تنبه.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He takes أرأيت as “tell me” and supplies omitted content: Joshua recalls what happened at the rock, is startled by forgetting the fish, and asks Moses about it.
rows.anchor: لما طلب موسى الحوت ذكر يوشع ما رأى منه وما اعتراه

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The author endorses the objection that al-Zamakhsharī’s “tell me” analysis lacks both the requested object and the required interrogative clause described by al-Akhfash.
rows.anchor: لا بد بعدها من الاسم المستخبر عنه ولزوم الاستفهام
